dedupe_keys.name: flowminder population and mobility estimates from mobile network data hdx collection

description: The Flowminder Foundation publishes on the Humanitarian Data Exchange population and mobility estimates it derives from pseudonymised call detail records of mobile operators, for disasters, epidemics and poverty mapping. The ten datasets listed on 26 September 2026 include monthly estimates of residents and relocations for 387 health zones of the Democratic Republic of Congo from March 2020 to April 2026; cohort mobility from the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak zones in Ituri and Nord-Kivu, built from Vodacom Congo data and updated in September 2026; population movement after Hurricane Matthew in Haiti (three dates in 2016); abnormal movements after the April 2015 Nepal earthquake; 1 km poverty estimates for Bangladesh from phone and satellite data; and Digicel Haiti network functionality after Hurricane Matthew. Coverage: DRC, Haiti, Nepal and Bangladesh at health-zone, commune or admin 3 and 4 levels. Format and access: CSV with variable lists, shapefiles and PDF reports, free to download from HDX under CC BY or CC BY-IGO. Caveats: subscriber cohorts are not the whole population; operator market share, phone ownership and a continuity model shape the numbers; raw records are never released. Simulation uses: agent-based and emergency-response models of displacement after hazards, exposure of people to outages, and validation of mobility models. Related records: the Italian mobile network population dataset and the Telecom Italia Big Data Challenge are European counterparts; NetEventSimulator makes synthetic events for testing these methods.
